subject: POC trial environment selection and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finedge.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finedge.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: POC trial environment selection and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya 


Thanks again for the demo and the productive discovery earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your POC (trial) started quickly:

Summary & success criteria (as we captured)
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 250ms for 1k qps simulated load
- Cost target: <= $0.0006 per generated token equivalent under the test workload
- Accuracy: top-3 intent classification match rate >= 92% on your eval set
- Stability: no dropped requests under a 30-minute sustained load test

Evaluation plan (recommended)
1) Environment setup (choose one):
   - Hosted Redwood trial (fastest): minimal setup, use hosted API with RBAC keys. Good if you don't need VPC/network controls.
   - Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput, we can pin a model/instance shape for the test. Requires billing commit for the sandbox window.
   - VPC trial (recommended given your data residency/network constraints): private VPC peering, customer-managed network controls, and optional customer-side private endpoints. This adds ~3-5 business days for network and firewall setup.

2) Baseline tests: small synthetic load to validate connectivity and baseline latencies
3) Feature tests: run your eval prompt set + streaming and tool-calling scenarios
4) Scale test: ramp to target qps and run 30-minute stability test
5) Final review: results, recommendations, and next steps for production rollout

Proposed timeline (flexible)
- Week 0 (this week): confirm environment choice + sign PoC agreement (DocuSign link below)
- Week 1: environment provisioning and technical kickoff
- Week 2: baseline + feature tests complete
- Week 3: scale test, results review, and decision point

Owners
- Redwood AE / engagement lead: Rachel Kim (cc'd) - commercial & scheduling
- Redwood Solutions / technical lead: Dylan Brooks (cc'd) - infra, onboarding, tests
- Customer technical lead: Alex Johnson - network and eval ownership

Action items for you
- Please confirm which environment you prefer (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC trial)
- If choosing VPC trial: share primary network contact and preferred maintenance window for peering (UTC offsets)
- Send initial eval prompt set and a small sample of expected payload sizes (for token/cost modeling)

Attachments: poc-requirements.pdf (short checklist), redwood-trial-guide.pdf (steps + runbook), vpc-worksheet.xlsx (network details we'll need)
DocuSign (POC agreement): https://www.docuSign.com/en/DEAL-2026-1192

If we get confirmation today, Rachel and I can lock in a kickoff for Mon/Tue next week.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Thanks Marissa - very clear, appreciate the recap. A few quick answers and questions: 

1) We'd prefer the VPC trial given our compliance and network restrictions (customer-managed egress rules and logging).
2) Success criteria look right to us; we'll confirm the eval prompt set by EOD tomorrow.
3) Timeline: can we aim to start kickoff next Mon (Nov 9)? That should give us time to align network folks. If VPC peering takes longer on your side, we can do an interim hosted baseline test in parallel.

One question: who at Redwood will own the peering config and can provide the network IP ranges / docs? Also need to confirm whether Redwood supports our required TLS mutual auth for outbound connections (we can share specifics).

- Nov 9 (kickoff): Technical kickoff call (Redwood: Marissa / Dylan / infra engineer; FinEdge: Alex + network lead)
- Nov 10-14: Baseline + feature tests (we'll run streaming and tool call scenarios against your prompt set)
- Nov 15: Scale/stability test & results review (final decision point)

Owners (explicit)

- Redwood technical lead: Dylan Brooks - VPC peering coordination, infra readiness, test harness

Customer deliverables required to start (please share by EOD Nov 6)

- Network contact name + email + preferred maintenance window
- Eval prompt set and 100 sample payloads (for token sizing)

Redwood deliverables
- VPC peering IP ranges and runbook (by Nov 8)
- Trial environment access + test harness instructions + sample curl commands
- A short test checklist (poc-requirements.pdf) to run during baseline tests

Attachments included: redwood-trial-guide.pdf (runbook), vpc-worksheet.xlsx (network details)

If Nov 9 works for you I'll schedule the kickoff and invite our infra engineer. Rachel - can you please draft the PoC SOW and DocuSign for signature? Dylan - can you block 45 minutes on Nov 9 for the kickoff and prepare the peering checklist?
